recap.headline: Chris and Tymko Post 2-0 Weeks as Three-Way Tie Forms at Top
recap.dek: Only two entrants managed clean sweeps in Week 2, with Chris and Tymko sitting tied with Orest at 3-1 overall. Three head-to-heads delivered decisive swings while the bottom of the standings grows crowded.
takeaways: Chris grabbed sole possession of the Week 2 honours with wins in both games, including a head-to-head demolition of Jordy's Lions that saw Josh Allen throw three touchdowns and James Cook III rush for 135 yards.

Tymko matched the 2-0 performance, getting a nail-biter from the Chiefs and a blowout from the Rams — Mahomes threw for 382 yards in Kansas City's 33-30 escape while Stafford carved up the Giants for four touchdowns.

Three head-to-heads went decisive: Chris over Jordy in Buffalo, Adrian over Bill in Foxborough, and Jordy over Matej in Denver. Adrian's Patriots blanked Bill's Steelers while holding Aaron Rodgers to 187 yards.
Ben's Texans remain winless at 0-2 after getting boat-raced by Cincinnati, but his Niners are perfect at 2-0 following Brock Purdy's surgical 20-for-22 dismantling of Miami.

games.text:
Chris's Bills survived a shootout with Jordy's Lions in the week's highest-scoring affair, pulling away late behind Josh Allen's three-touchdown performance and James Cook III's 135-yard rushing clinic. Jared Goff threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns in a losing effort, with Amon-Ra St. Brown hauling in nine catches for 142 yards and two scores, but the Lions' 31 points weren't nearly enough to keep pace with Buffalo's explosive attack.

The head-to-head victory gives Chris a crucial edge over Jordy in the standings — both sit at 2-2 overall, but Chris holds the tiebreaker should it come to that. Jordy's Lions will try to bounce back Sunday afternoon against the Jets, while Chris faces a massive Week 3 clash Thursday night when his Packers host Atlanta before the Bills take on Taras's Chargers in another head-to-head Sunday.

Taras's Panthers absolutely obliterated Atlanta in what might be the most lopsided result of the young season, holding the Falcons to a field goal while Bryce Young threw three touchdowns in a 287-yard afternoon. The Panthers' defence was suffocating — Atlanta managed just 86 passing yards with two interceptions, and the Falcons never threatened after halftime.

The blowout keeps Taras afloat at 1-3 despite his Chargers dropping their second straight. Carolina faces a quick turnaround with a trip to Cleveland on Sunday, while the Chargers desperately need a win when they visit Chris's Bills in a head-to-head that could make or break both entrants' early-season hopes.

Matej's Eagles escaped Tennessee with a narrow victory despite Jalen Hurts throwing two interceptions to go along with his two touchdowns. DeVonta Smith caught ten passes for 117 yards and a score, and the Eagles' defence held on late after the Titans threatened to complete a comeback.

The win keeps Matej's Eagles perfect at 2-0, offsetting the disappointing loss his Jaguars took in Denver. Philadelphia gets a Monday night showcase in Week 3 against Chicago, while the Jags will try to regroup when Adrian's Patriots come to Jacksonville in what shapes up as a pivotal head-to-head.

Adrian's Patriots dismantled Bill's Steelers in Foxborough, holding Pittsburgh to a field goal in a head-to-head rout that saw Aaron Rodgers struggle mightily — 187 yards, an interception, and absolutely no rhythm. Drake Maye wasn't spectacular either, throwing a pick of his own, but Tyler Henderson's 76-yard rushing day and a touchdown were more than enough.

The head-to-head win is massive for Adrian, who sits at 1-3 but now holds the edge over Bill in any tiebreaker scenario. Bill's Steelers managed just 43 rushing yards and couldn't establish anything offensively. The Patriots face another head-to-head Sunday when they travel to Jacksonville to face Matej's Jags, while Bill's Steelers host Cincinnati looking to avoid an 0-2 start to the pool at home.

Chris's Packers grinded out a three-point road win over the Jets behind Jordan Love's two-touchdown afternoon, overcoming Geno Smith's 247-yard effort for New York. The Packers' offence wasn't explosive — 145 passing yards and 32 rushing yards from Kimani Johnson — but it was just enough to escape MetLife Stadium with the W.

The narrow victory gives Chris his second win of the week and puts him squarely in the three-way tie atop the standings. Green Bay gets a short week, hosting Atlanta on Thursday night in Week 3, while the Bills face Taras's Chargers on Sunday in a head-to-head that could create some separation in the middle of the pack.

Adrian's Buccaneers fell to Cleveland in a game they desperately needed, with Baker Mayfield throwing an interception and the offence never quite finding its rhythm despite Bucky Irving's 89-yard rushing performance. Deshaun Watson threw two touchdowns for the Browns, and Tampa's defence couldn't get the stop it needed late.

The loss drops Adrian's Bucs to 0-2 and puts real pressure on his Patriots to deliver next week. Tampa hosts Minnesota on Sunday afternoon in what's becoming a must-win situation if Adrian wants to stay within striking distance of the middle of the pack.

Orest's Ravens couldn't hold off New Orleans at home, falling in a game where Lamar Jackson threw for 235 yards and a touchdown but also tossed a costly interception. Derrick Henry rushed for 68 yards and a score, but it wasn't enough to overcome Tyler Shough's efficient 27-for-34 performance for the Saints.

The loss spoils what would have been a perfect week for Orest, whose Seahawks demolished Arizona 31-7. Baltimore travels to face Bill's Cowboys in a Week 3 head-to-head on Sunday afternoon that could swing momentum heading into the heart of the season.

Ben's Texans looked downright lost in Houston, managing just two field goals despite C.J. Stroud throwing for 353 yards on 55 attempts. Joe Burrow and the Bengals controlled the game wire-to-wire, with Chase Brown rushing for 80 yards and Burrow connecting on two touchdowns to cruise past a Texans offence that couldn't finish drives.

The loss drops Houston to 0-2 and puts Ben in a precarious spot despite his Niners sitting pretty at 2-0. The Texans travel to Indianapolis on Sunday looking to salvage something before the early deficit becomes insurmountable.

Jordy's Broncos held off Matej's Jaguars in a head-to-head that saw Bo Nix throw for 288 yards and Jaylen Waddle catch eight passes for 138 yards in Denver's seven-point win. Trevor Lawrence struggled for Jacksonville, throwing an interception and managing just 189 yards as the Jags' offence sputtered.

The head-to-head win salvages Jordy's week after his Lions got torched in Buffalo, keeping him at 2-2 overall. The Broncos host Tymko's Rams on Sunday night in another head-to-head that could shake up the standings, while Matej's Jags get a chance to rebound against Adrian's Patriots in a head-to-head of their own.

Taras's Chargers dropped their second straight, falling at home to Las Vegas in a game where Justin Herbert threw two interceptions and the offence never found its rhythm. Kirk Cousins threw three touchdowns for the Raiders, and despite Omarion Hampton rushing for 94 yards, the Chargers couldn't keep pace.

The loss drops the Chargers to 0-2 and puts Taras in a hole despite his Panthers' blowout win earlier in the day. Los Angeles travels to face Chris's Bills on Sunday in a must-win head-to-head — another loss would all but bury Taras's playoff hopes before October arrives.

Bill's Cowboys demolished Washington behind Dak Prescott's four-touchdown masterpiece, with CeeDee Lamb catching eight passes for 153 yards and two scores in a performance that makes you wonder if Dallas might be legitimate this year. The Cowboys' defence held Jayden Daniels to 69 rushing yards and kept the Commanders out of the end zone until garbage time.

The win salvages Bill's week after his Steelers got blanked in New England, keeping him at 2-2 overall. Dallas hosts Orest's Ravens on Sunday afternoon in a head-to-head that could vault the winner toward the top of the standings or drop the loser into the crowded middle.

Orest's Seahawks absolutely dismantled Arizona in the desert, with Drew Lock throwing three touchdowns and Jaxon Smith-Njigba catching nine passes for 155 yards and all three scores in a performance that puts Seattle firmly in the 2-0 club. The Cardinals managed just 95 passing yards and never threatened after the first quarter.

The blowout keeps Orest tied atop the standings at 3-1 despite his Ravens' disappointing loss to New Orleans. Seattle travels to Washington on Sunday afternoon before Orest's Ravens face Bill's Cowboys in a Sunday evening head-to-head that could create some separation at the top.

Ben's Niners rolled past Miami behind Brock Purdy's surgical 20-for-22 performance for 287 yards and two touchdowns, with George Kittle catching four passes for 80 yards and a score. Purdy added a rushing touchdown, and the Niners' defence held Miami's offence in check all afternoon despite De'Von Achane rushing for 74 yards.

The win keeps San Francisco perfect at 2-0 and gives Ben something to hang his hat on while his Texans sit winless. The Niners host Arizona on Sunday afternoon looking to move to 3-0 and keep Ben in striking distance of the leaders despite Houston's early struggles.

Tymko's Chiefs survived Indianapolis in a thriller that saw Patrick Mahomes throw for 382 yards and three touchdowns while Kenneth Walker III rushed for 117 yards to outlast Jonathan Taylor's two-touchdown performance for the Colts. Travis Kelce caught nine passes for 101 yards and a score, and Kansas City's offence did just enough to hold off a late Indianapolis rally.

The nail-biter gives Tymko his first win of the week and keeps the Chiefs unbeaten at 2-0. Kansas City travels to Miami on Sunday before Tymko's Rams host Jordy's Broncos on Sunday night in a head-to-head that could vault the winner into outright first place.

Tymko's Rams demolished the Giants behind Matthew Stafford's four-touchdown explosion, with Davante Adams catching eight passes for 195 yards and two scores in a performance that sent New York packing. The Giants managed just 111 passing yards and a pair of field goals, never threatening after the first quarter.

The blowout gives Tymko a perfect 2-0 week and puts him in the three-way tie atop the standings at 3-1. The Rams travel to face Jordy's Broncos on Sunday night in a head-to-head that could create some real separation — the winner moves to 4-1 while the loser falls to 2-2 and out of the top tier.

He sits tied for first at 3-1 but faces a massive Week 3 with his Seahawks traveling to Washington on Sunday afternoon before his Ravens visit Bill's Cowboys in a Sunday evening head-to-head.

Jordy won a head-to-head in Denver but his Lions got torched by Chris's Bills. Matej's Eagles survived Tennessee but his Jags lost the head-to-head to Jordy. All five face critical Week 3 matchups with four head-to-heads among them.

Sunday night brings Tymko's Rams to face Jordy's Broncos in a head-to-head between two 2-2 entrants, while Sunday afternoon features three more head-to-heads: Adrian's Patriots at Matej's Jags, Orest's Ravens at Bill's Cowboys, and a potential statement game as Orest's 2-0 Seahawks travel to Washington.

recaps.headline: Matej and Orest sweep opening week; Taras gets buried
recaps.dek: Only two entrants managed clean 2-0 starts as head-to-heads decided half the pool's opening slate. Matej edges Orest on net points for the early lead, while Taras and Adrian share the basement at 0-2.
takeaways: Three head-to-heads in Week 1, and all three went to the visitor — road warriors indeed.
Matej's Jags hung 34 on Cleveland in a Trevor Lawrence masterclass. Four touchdowns on 18-of-23 passing? That'll play.
The Ravens put up 41 on Indy behind Derrick Henry's three rushing scores. Orest's squad looking scary early.
Taras endured a 96-point shellacking across both teams. His Panthers gave up 59 to Chicago in a game that got out of hand fast.

games.text:
Orest's Seahawks squeaked past Adrian's Patriots 13-10 in a defensive slugfest that saw Drew Lock manage the game efficiently (16-of-22, 187 yards, 1 TD) while Drake Maye threw three picks in his debut. Jaxon Smith-Njigba hauled in eight catches for 122 yards and the lone Seattle touchdown, while the Pats managed just 51 rushing yards on 18 Rhamondre Stevenson carries. The game never found much offensive rhythm — New England's lone score came late, and Adrian's offense sputtered all afternoon.

The head-to-head meant Orest banked a point while Adrian fell to 0-1 on his AFC side. Not the start either quarterback wanted, but Orest will take the win and the early advantage.

Ben's Niners dismantled Tymko's Rams 27-7 in Los Angeles, with Brock Purdy carving up the Rams secondary for three touchdowns on 25-of-34 passing. Christian McCaffrey added 68 yards on the ground and Demario Robinson caught a 50-yard score as San Francisco controlled the game from start to finish. Matthew Stafford managed just 155 yards on 15-of-25 passing with a pick, and the Rams offense never found any kind of rhythm — Puka Nacua's 74 yards on five catches were the lone bright spot.

The head-to-head handed Ben a crucial win on his NFC side while Tymko dropped to 0-1 with the Rams. With his Chiefs taking care of business later in the week, Tymko salvaged a 1-1 split, but this one stung.

Adrian's Bucs fell 33-27 in Cincinnati despite Baker Mayfield's efficient 23-of-28 performance. Joe Burrow threw for 254 yards and a score while Chase Brown punched in a rushing touchdown, and the Bengals pulled away late. Bucky Irving added a touchdown on the ground for Tampa, but it wasn't enough to overcome the home team's balanced attack.

Adrian drops to 0-2 after dropping both his opening weekend games, and the net points are starting to stack up against him early.

Jordy's Lions survived a wild shootout 31-30 over New Orleans, with Jahmyr Gibbs ripping off 156 yards and two touchdowns on 29 carries. Jared Goff connected with Amon-Ra St. Brown ten times for 67 yards and two scores in a game that saw the Saints' Travis Shough throw for 410 yards and three touchdowns on 35-of-56 passing. Chris Olave hauled in 10 catches for 182 yards for New Orleans, but the Saints couldn't quite get over the hump.

Jordy needed every yard Gibbs could muster to escape with the win. With his Broncos getting throttled later in the week, this narrow victory kept him at 1-1 instead of staring down an 0-2 hole.

Orest's Ravens absolutely demolished Indianapolis 41-23, with Derrick Henry bulldozing his way to 144 yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries. Lamar Jackson was surgical through the air (17-of-25, 324 yards, 1 TD) and Zay Flowers torched the Colts secondary for 150 yards and a score on just five catches. Jonathan Taylor tried to keep Indy in it with 98 yards and two touchdowns on the ground, but the Ravens were simply too much.

Orest's 2-0 start looks dominant — his two teams outscored opponents by a combined 21 points, second only to Matej's 26. The Ravens look like a legitimate contender early.

Bill's Steelers ground out a 20-13 win over Atlanta as Aaron Rodgers threw for 221 yards and a touchdown on 24-of-40 passing. The Pittsburgh defense forced two picks off Cooper Rush, who managed just 143 yards on 12-of-22 passing. Bijan Robinson carried the Falcons with 83 yards rushing and another 90 receiving plus a touchdown, but Atlanta couldn't overcome the turnovers.

Bill picked up the win on his AFC side, though his Cowboys would drop their game later to leave him at 1-1. The Steelers defense looks stout early, which could be a theme this season.

Taras's Panthers got absolutely demolished 59-37 in Chicago, with D'Andre Swift rumbling for 124 yards and three touchdowns as the Bears offense clicked on all cylinders. Caleb Williams threw for 269 yards and two scores on 21-of-29 passing, and Chicago hung 59 on Carolina in a game that was never competitive. Bryce Young threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns in garbage time, and Jalen Coker added 138 yards and two scores, but the Panthers defense was Swiss cheese all afternoon.

Taras started the season in the worst possible way — his Panthers gave up 59, and his Chargers would lose later to complete an 0-2 opening week with a brutal minus-34 net points. Nowhere to go but up.

Matej's Jaguars throttled Cleveland 34-10 behind a vintage Trevor Lawrence performance — 18-of-23 for 245 yards and four touchdowns. Brenton Tuten added 66 yards on the ground and Perry Washington hauled in a score as Jacksonville's offense looked unstoppable. Deshaun Watson threw for 205 yards and a touchdown for the Browns, but Cleveland's offense sputtered and the defense had no answers.

Matej's Jags looked like a legitimate threat in Week 1, and combined with his Eagles' narrow win, he sits atop the pool at 2-0 with a plus-26 net. Early statement made.

Chris's Bills outlasted Ben's Texans 36-31 in a high-scoring affair, with Josh Allen throwing for 334 yards and two touchdowns on 20-of-29 passing. Dalton Kincaid went off for 130 yards on five catches, and the Bills offense clicked despite James Cook managing just 57 yards on the ground. C.J. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two scores for Houston, and David Montgomery punched in two rushing touchdowns, but the Texans couldn't quite keep pace.

The head-to-head handed Chris a point on his AFC side while Ben dropped to 0-1 with the Texans. Chris salvaged a 1-1 week despite his Packers getting walloped, while Ben's Niners blowout kept him in the same boat.

Chris's Packers got throttled 39-22 in Minnesota despite Jordan Love throwing for 387 yards and two touchdowns on 21-of-42 passing. Christian Watson caught six balls for 147 yards and two scores, but the Pack defense couldn't stop Carson Wentz (3 TDs) or Justin Jefferson (8 catches, 92 yards, 2 TDs). Jordan Mason added a rushing touchdown for the Vikings, and Minnesota controlled the game throughout.

Chris drops to 0-1 on his NFC side, and the minus-17 point differential in this one stung. Combined with his Bills win, he sits at 1-1 with a minus-12 net.

Matej's Eagles squeaked past Washington 24-22 as Jalen Hurts threw three touchdown passes on 14-of-25 passing. Dallas Goedert hauled in two of those scores, and Saquon Barkley added 83 yards on the ground as Philadelphia held on late. Jayden Daniels threw for 164 yards and two touchdowns for Washington, and Javonte Croskey-Merritt punched in a rushing score, but the Commanders came up just short.

The narrow win gave Matej a clean 2-0 sweep and pole position in the pool. His Eagles didn't dominate, but two points is two points.

Taras's Chargers fell 26-14 to Arizona as Jacoby Brissett threw for 277 yards and a touchdown on 27-of-37 passing. Trey McBride caught nine balls for 95 yards and a score, and Tyler Allgeier added 61 yards on the ground as the Cardinals controlled the game. Justin Herbert managed 209 yards for the Chargers but threw a pick, and Omarion Hampton scored a rushing touchdown, but Los Angeles couldn't overcome the deficit.

Taras drops to 0-2 after his Chargers joined his Panthers in the loss column. The minus-34 net points have him in a deep hole already.

Bill's Cowboys fell 28-20 to the Giants as Jaxson Dart threw for 230 yards and three touchdowns on 23-of-29 passing. Cam Skattebo rumbled for 81 yards and a score, and Isaiah Likely caught two touchdown passes as the G-men dominated. Dak Prescott threw for 175 yards and two scores for Dallas but also tossed a pick, and CeeDee Lamb was held to just 44 yards on five catches.

Bill drops to 0-1 on his NFC side, and the loss cost him a chance at a 2-0 start. He sits at 1-1 with a minus-1 net after his Steelers saved the week.

Tymko's Chiefs rolled over Jordy's Broncos 31-10 in Kansas City, with Kenneth Walker III absolutely gashing Denver for 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries. Patrick Mahomes threw for 184 yards and two scores despite a pick, and Travis Kelce added 71 yards on three catches. Bo Nix managed just 131 yards for the Broncos and threw a pick, and J.K. Dobbins was held to 36 yards on eight carries as Denver's offense never got going.

The head-to-head handed Tymko a point while Jordy dropped to 0-1 on his AFC side. Tymko salvaged a 1-1 week after his Rams got blown out, while Jordy's narrow Lions win kept him at 1-1 despite the shellacking his Broncos endured.
